title: More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait
text: More on tanker set ablaze in Hormuz Strait A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by a small boat with two explosive devices attached to its hull, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said in an update on Friday. This caused blasts and sparked a fire in the vessel's engine room that temporarily disabled it. According to UKMTO, the crew were safe, there was no environmental impact and the fire had been extinguished. The vessel is now continuing to its next port of call. There was no immediate answer as to who was behind the attack. Earlier, we reported that the tanker, transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz, was on fire. The incident occurred 25 nautical miles north east of Oman's Khasab.

title: Can Netanyahu cling onto power (again)?
text: Can Netanyahu cling onto power (again)? Israel's election has ended in deadlock. Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats, his rival Gadi Eisenkot's 48, and neither has the 61 needed to govern. The surprise of the night: Palestinian citizens of Israel turned out in record numbers, pushing Arab parties to a record 19 seats. They did so despite armed right-wing observers in their towns and a campaign of fear from the prime minister. Now Netanyahu's Likud claims the election was "stolen" by Arab parties. Police say there is no evidence. Arab parties offer to back an anti-Netanyahu government, but the Zionist opposition is wary of relying on them. So who will govern Israel, and could deadlock keep Netanyahu in power anyway? Middle East Eye Live’s Mathilda Mallinson and James Schneider speak to Joint List MK Ofer Cassif, MEE's Lubna Masarwa, and former Israeli negotiator Daniel Levy.

title: Vance says Trump will not allow US conflict in Iran to turn into a 'forever war'

The United States has been dealing with Iran for 47 years, and I promise you that Donald Trump is not going to let Iran become a forever war."

title: Report: US sends 10 military planes to Israel, amid plans for a possible military operation against Iran
text: Report: US sends 10 military planes to Israel, amid plans for a possible military operation against Iran The US has transferred 10 military cargo planes to Israeli air bases as preparation for a possible military operation against Iran, according to the Israeli public broadcaster KAN. The broadcaster said the aircraft landed at Ovda and Nevatim air bases in the southern Negev region. Several other aircrafts were reportedly dispatched elsewhere in the region, including Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. An Israeli official told KAN that Israel and the US are "coordinating closely, and although no decision has yet been made on the matter, the Americans and Israel are preparing for any decision President Donald Trump makes".

title: US envoy says Iran talks ‘very close’ to agreement on de-escalation process
text: US envoy says Iran talks ‘very close’ to agreement on de-escalation process US Ambassador to Turkey, Tom Barrack, said diplomatic efforts to ease tensions with Iran could bring “dramatic steps forward” within two weeks, though further US military action remains possible. Speaking to CNN, Barrack said Qatar, Pakistan and other US allies had brought the sides “very close” to an agreement on a process aimed at securing a temporary pause in hostilities. “We’re not going to have an overall solution immediately,” he said, stressing the need to “bring temperatures down”. Asked about a possible “short, sharp” US military operation against Iran, Barrack said President Donald Trump and his administration were seriously considering “kinetic action”.

title: Houthis claim six attacks on Saudi Arabia airports and oil facilities
text: Houthis claim six attacks on Saudi Arabia airports and oil facilities The Houthis carried out six attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting airports, oil facilities and a military headquarters, spokesperson Yahya Saree said. Saree said the group fired ballistic missiles at the Ras Tanura and Rabigh oil refineries, a missile at an Aramco facility in Abqaiq, and multiple missiles at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. He also said the group attacked King Fahd International Airport in Dammam with a drone and targeted the headquarters of Saudi troops in Najran. Saudi Arabia has yet to confirm the attacks.

title: Italy urges 'immediate release' of activists detained in West Bank
text: Italy urges 'immediate release' of activists detained in West Bank The Italian foreign ministry called on Thursday for the "immediate release" of five Italian activists detained in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. The activists were held near the village of Al-Lubban al-Gharbiyye, "where they were present alongside Palestinian farmers engaged in the olive harvest", said a ministry statement. "The Italian nationals were detained today during an operation that reportedly also involved other foreign citizens," it said. Rome is seeking "immediate clarification regarding the circumstances of the detention", the ministry said, adding that the Italians were being held at a police station.

title: US senator briefed on Trump's plans to restart Iran war says proposal is 'insane'
text: US senator briefed on Trump's plans to restart Iran war says proposal is 'insane' Senator Chris Murphy says he has been briefed on the US's plan to restart the war on Iran , calling it "insane" and saying it would lead to a "devastating escalation". "You've heard a preview that it would be a short-duration plan. I'll just say this: their plan is insane," Murphy said, speaking at an event organised by the Middle East Institute in Washington, DC, on Wednesday. "It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law." Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, made the comments after American media reported on Wednesday that the US warned several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military offensive against Iran after the US midterm elections on 3 November. title: Declared 38 years ago, denied since: the Algiers Declaration remains a milestone in the Palestinian struggle
text: On 15 November, 1988, in Algiers, Yasser Arafat, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), stood before the Palestine National Council, the PLO’s parliament-in-exile, and proclaimed the Palestinian Declaration of Independence. Some 75 countries recognised the declaration within a month, and more than 90 had done so by early 1989, giving the Palestinian national movement unprecedented diplomatic momentum. text: Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets. Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover “all hacking losses”. An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said. Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday. Bitcoin dropped more than 3 per cent to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3pc to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5pc over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8pc while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6pc in extended US trading. text: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan remained deeply hostile to journalism and its practitioners in 2025-26 despite a decline in documented violations against media workers, according to a new report issued by an Islamabad-based media watchdog. “About 10 cases a month [against media personnel], their nationwide spread and severity in the period showed that fewer violations did not mean greater safety,” stated Freedom Network’s latest annual Impunity Report 2026, titled “From Violence to Lawfare: Process as Punishment for Journalists”. title: IRIS access alone is not legal service, LHC rules
text: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court has held that merely uploading an appellate order to the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) Inland Revenue Information System (IRIS) does not constitute valid service under the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. An LHC division bench comprising Justice Mirza Viqas Rauf and Justice Anwaar Hussain decided three connected reference applications led by Tahir Mehmood. The applications challenged three orders of the Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue, which had dismissed the taxpayers’ appeals as time-barred on the ground that uploading the orders to IRIS constituted sufficient service. In one case, the taxpayer argued that Covid-19 and quarantine following a foreign trip had prevented him from accessing the portal. In the other two cases, the taxpayers said they learned of the Commissioner (Appeals)’ orders only after receiving recovery notices in April 2026, months after the orders had been passed. Justice Anwaar Hussain, who authored the judgement, held that Section 218(1)(d) of the ordinance recognises electronic service only when carried out in the prescribed manner. He observed that Rule 74 of the Income Tax Rules limits an electronic addr­e­ss to a fax number or an email address and requi­res confirmation of transmission. title: Sindh govt to launch internship programme for new graduates next month: Sharjeel
text: KARACHI: Sindh Senior Minister Sha­r­jeel Inam Memon has announ­ced that an internship programme for fresh graduates is being launched from next month through the iwork4Sindh platform. He said that the programme would provide young people with better opportunities to gain practical experience. He said the Sindh government is taking practical measures to provide employment opportunities to young people and enhance their professional capabilities. “The government wants young people to have an appropriate platform to utilise their abilities and access better opportunities,” he added. Mr Memon added that the next phase of physical short courses for skilled individuals is also being launched on the iwork4Sindh platform in collaboration with companies. These courses will focus on developing young people’s skills in accordance with market requirements, he said, adding that in the present era, traditional education alone is not sufficient, as practical skills and professional training are also of great importance to secure employment. Regarding the performance of the iwork4Sindh platform, the minister said that more than 5.3 million visits had been recorded on the platform so far, while the number of registered candidates had increased to 137,770 and the number of registered companies had reached 726. title: How exposed is Bangladesh to a prolonged Saudi crisis?
text: Bangladesh is unlikely to see an immediate fall in remittances from Saudi Arabia even as Houthi attacks on the kingdom intensified from early October, but a slowdown in new migration could weigh on inflows in the years ahead. Following the attacks, migration to Saudi Arabia, the largest destination for Bangladeshi workers, has already been disrupted. As of Sunday, 144 direct and transit flights had been affected by prolonged flight restrictions at Saudi airports, disrupting the travel plans of around 22,000 passengers. But economists and manpower experts say remittance inflows are unlikely to be hit immediately because newly arrived migrant workers typically take about a year to start sending significant amounts of money home. According to them, the longer-term impact will depend on the duration of the crisis, the performance of the Saudi economy and demand for labour, particularly in construction. A prolonged crisis that damages the Saudi economy could slow job creation and reduce workers’ incomes. But the outcome is not necessarily negative for the kingdom’s economy. If Houthi missile and drone attacks continue without damaging oilfields and refineries, higher global oil prices could boost Saudi revenues, potentially supporting investment and demand for foreign workers, according to Zahid Hussain, a former lead economist at the World Bank’s Dhaka office. “But everything is uncertain so far,” he commented. text: • CPPA seeks Rs2.56 per unit additional fuel cost adjustment to recover Rs33bn • Industrial representatives insist fuel levies inflating generation costs ISLAMABAD: The manufacturing sector and the power division on Thursday unanimously called for the removal or reduction of the petroleum levy on furnace oil and diesel used for power generation, stressing that it was resulting in about Rs10 per unit additional impact to electricity costs. The demand emerged during a public hearing on the Rs2.56 per unit additional monthly fuel cost adjustment (FCA) sought by power companies to recover about Rs33 billion for electricity consumed in September. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) conducted the hearing on a request by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) to allow distribution companies to charge the additional FCA in November bills. A government official said the proposed adjustment was the highest for comparable months in recent years. Industrial representatives Amir Shaikh, Arif Bilwani, Tanveer Bari and Rehan Javed, representing various chambers of commerce and industry, said the government was charging substantial petroleum levies — about Rs76,000 per tonne on furnace oil and Rs80 per litre on diesel — which could otherwise be reduced to lower generation costs amid the energy crisis arising from the Iran conflict. title: Pakistan, Turkiye shall 'continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy' alongside bolstering defences: PM Shehbaz
text: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday affirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye would continue to push for dialogue and diplomacy while strengthening their defences under the Makkah Defence Agreement. He made the remarks while addressing an event in Islamabad marking the 103rd national day of Turkiye, with which Pakistan enjoys strong bilateral ties and maintains multi-sectoral cooperation. The premier said the pact, signed on Aug 7 between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, marked an “important milestone” in cooperation between Islamabad and Ankara. “It strengthens our collective deterrence and reinforces our shared commitment to regional peace and stability,” PM Shehbaz noted. “While we strengthen our defences, we shall continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy, respect for international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.” The prime minister hailed Turkiye’s diplomatic support during Marka-i-Haq last May, when India initiated unilateral aggression against Pakistan, triggering a four-day conflict between the nuclear-armed neighbours. “Turkiye stood firmly by our side with unwavering commitment and dedication. This sincere act of solidarity was a profound source of comfort and strength for the people of Pakistan, a gesture that will forever remain etched in our hearts and our memories,” he emphasised. title: Nuclear jingoism
text: INDIA’S nuclear jingoism was on ample display during Operation Marka-i-Haq in May 2025 when it fired dual-use BrahMos cruise missiles with conventional payload, unmindful of the fact that the dangerous caper could have been misconstrued by Pakistani air defenders as a nuclear attack. Despite an agreement on pre-notification of flight testing of ballistic missiles, the Indians, while testing the Agni V MIRV-capable missile, have shown a blithe disregard for established pre-notification protocols that mandate a 72-hour pre-test notification, a fact pointed out by Pakistan’s Foreign Office in 2024. While the Indians keep up an implacable momentum of vertical proliferation of nuclear and missile technology, the world indulges them through exceptionalism enshrined in the nuclear waiver for the Nuclear Suppliers Group and membership of the Missile Technology Control Regime. The Indians have slyly wangled the concession from the USA and IAEA in the civil nuclear deal to keep eight reactors out of IAEA oversight. These pressurised heavy water reactors consume less nuclear fuel than they produce, which can be harvested for strategic military purposes. It should be remembered that it was the Indians who introduced the nuclear arms race in the subcontinent because of their grandiose big-power pretensions. text: Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran. title: Quintessential capitalism
text: FEW companies are hailed as proof of free-market genius more than Tesla. Yet, at every turn that mattered, it stood on public capital. In 2010 it borrowed $465m from a US federal programme open to every carmaker building cleaner vehicles, in a country where transport is now the largest source of greenhouse gases. It paid the Treasury’s own cost, roughly one to 3.4 per cent, with principal deferred until production began. One of the smallest borrowers, it became the star, repaying with interest nine years early. Regulatory credits, earned by beating emission rules and bought by those that fall short, then carried it into profit. Pakistan asks its banks to do alone what no quintessential capitalist economy asks of its own: lend to priority sectors without the state sharing the risk and the price. This is not a lesson taken from state-led economies such as China, where public support is part of the model. It comes from the market economies themselves, which do it openly and without apology. Tesla is not their exception; it is their method. Look at where they aim interest subsidies, and how deep. Farming comes first: America lends beginning farmers money to buy land at under 2pc and caps their operating microloans at 5pc, while Canada pays the interest on the first C$250,000 of each grower’s cash advance. title: Pakistan’s climate defences under scrutiny amid Lancet warning
text: • Ex-health officials slam country’s ‘too little, too late’ disaster response; demand climate-proof hospitals, early warnings, heat action plans • Study calls for climate change to be declared global health emergency • Heat-related deaths rise 36pc since Paris accord; economic losses estimated at over $1tr ISLAMABAD: Health and environmental experts in Pakistan have called for urgent measures to address growing climate-related health risks after a Lancet report warned that rising heat-related deaths, floods, droughts and economic losses are outpacing global efforts to combat climate change. The 2026 Lancet Countdown report, launched at the British Library in London, called for climate change to be recognised as a “global health emergency”, warning that climate-related health risks continue to worsen a decade after the Paris Agreement. The report found that average annual heat-related deaths worldwide have risen 36 per cent since the Paris Agreement. In 2023, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths, with more than 70pc attributed to human-caused climate change. Meanwhile, heat-related economic losses reached an estimated $1.07 trillion in 2025. title: Candid admission
text: PARLIAMENT has recently been debating the future of Pakistani democracy, but those debates will be for naught unless our leaders also develop the capacity to acknowledge each other’s positions. The past two days have seen the government and opposition benches trading blame for democracy’s present, rather sorry state. On Wednesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures. He also said his party was “prepared to die” resisting the government if the latter continued pursuing a policy of confrontation and violence, and proposed a new Charter of Democracy as the way out. Regretting that his efforts to mediate between the government and the PTI had failed because the government had changed course and imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in KP, the maulana said the political leadership had grown too intolerant for parliament to do its job. He was not wrong, though the fault is hardly the government’s alone. The maulana’s rebuke drew two kinds of response. title: Pakistan 'overperformer' in innovation, climbs 4 ranks globally in 2026: report
text: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan rose to 95th place among the 139 economies of the world featured in the ‘Global Innovation Index 2026’ published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), it emerged on Thursday. Advancing in rank from 99th place in 2025, Pakistan also reclaimed its “overperformer” status for the fourth time, a status given to economies identified as performing above expectations for their level of economic development. It also held the status in 2022 and 2024. The global index report showed that Pakistan performed better in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2026. This year, Pakistan ranked 121st in innovation inputs and 72nd in innovation outputs — both higher than last year. “Innovation overperformance shows that innovation does not follow a straight line from income to results,” the report said. “The 2026 overperformers show that economies can generate more innovation than expected for their level of development when they build on focused strengths.” A list of countries that performed above expectations for their level of development in innovation in 2026, according to the Global Innovation Index 2026. — screengrab from WIPO report WIPO highlighted that Pakistan’s strengths were concentrated in the digital economy , particularly mobile app creation, ICT services exports, high-tech imports, and software spending. title: Rising interest payments, uplift spending strained Pakistan's fiscal position in early FY27: ministry
text: ISLAMABAD: Despite a massive 90 per cent cut in subsidies and higher-than-targeted revenue collection, Pakistan’s fiscal and current account buffers weakened at the beginning of the current fiscal year (FY27) owing to an almost 37pc increase in interest payments coupled with greater development spending. The “overall fiscal surplus narrowed to 0.8pc of GDP (Rs1.198 trillion), compared with 1.7pc of GDP (Rs2.124tr)” in the corresponding period of FY26, said the Ministry of Finance’s Monthly Economic Update & Outlook report issued on Thursday. “Similarly, the primary surplus declined to 1.6pc of GDP (Rs2.3tr), from 2.3pc of GDP (Rs2.94tr) recorded in the same period last year,” it added in the report’s October edition. The government, however, pledged to keep fiscal policy focused on preserving stability through stronger revenue mobilisation and prudent expenditure management. The report said the overall fiscal operations began on a positive note in FY27 as tax revenues surpassed target. Net federal revenue amounted to Rs2.9123 trillion, exceeding federal expenditure of Rs2.124tr. This contributed to a federal fiscal surplus equivalent to 0.5pc. The Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) tax collection posted 3.6pc growth during July-August. title: Afghanistan's Rashid Khan becomes first men's player to claim 200 T20I wickets
text: Former Afghanistan captain Rashid Khan became the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in men’s Twenty20 Internationals on Thursday, reaching the milestone during Afghanistan’s second T20 against Zimbabwe in Sharjah. The leg-spinner brought up the landmark when he trapped Tadiwanashe Marumani lbw for two in the ninth over. Rashid achieved the feat in his 120th T20 international, with the 28-year-old boasting an average of 13.96 and an economy rate of 6.13 in the format. His record includes two five-wicket hauls, with best figures of 5-3. The Afghan sits comfortably atop the list of leading wicket-takers in men’s T20 internationals with 200 wickets, 29 clear of England’s Adil Rashid in second place. Rashid Khan became the first Afghanistan bowler to reach 200 ODI wickets during a match against Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi in October last year.

title: US stocks slide as Google parent's revenue miss revives AI spending jitters
text: US stock prices retreated on Thursday, with investors reassessing big tech’s massive AI spending spree as they digested high-profile earnings, crucial inflation data and the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision. All three major US stock indexes were in negative territory, with the Nasdaq dragged sharply lower by tech and tech-related megacaps in the wake of Alphabet’s disappointing quarterly results released late Wednesday. In contrast, the smallcap Russell 2000 advanced 0.8 per cent. Semiconductor stocks were poised to snap their four-day winning streak, dropping 2.0pc as investors sought to distinguish between companies that can fund their lofty AI ambitions from those that burn through cash and borrow funds to realise their ambitions. Alphabet was in the latter camp following its quarterly report released late on Wednesday. The Google parent’s revenue miss was compounded by its accelerated AI-related cash burn. Its shares slid 13.2pc. “A risk-off day like this, with small caps outperforming, is a good sign that thus far the market’s interpretation of cracks in the AI story doesn’t mean cracks in every corner of the market,” said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. “There’s plenty of other places to go with your money outside of the AI trade that have pretty decent prospects.” On Wednesday, Federal Reserve policymakers chose to hold US rates steady, acknowledging that while price pressures remain “elevated”, the central bank will dec

title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
text: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. A formal trial commenced after both lawyers pleaded not guilty. Both were on bail in this case prior to the verdict. Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict in the case at Adiala jail on Thursday, where the trial was conducted. The sentence was handed down under three separate legal provisions. According to the judgment, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the two were sentenced to ten years along with a fine of Rs100,000 each under Section 7 (h) of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, as defined under Section 6 (2) (m) — serious coercion or intimidation of a public servant in order to force him to discharge or to refrain from discharging his lawful duties. The court further handed down a one-year sentence and fined Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). title: Rana Sanaullah says Imran's jailed sister Noreen 'fine' after being provided medical treatment
text: Adviser to the prime minister on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, on Thursday informed the Senate that Noreen Niazi, the sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, was fine after being provided medical treatment in Lahore. Speaking on the floor of the Senate on Thursday, Sanaullah responded to the query by PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Ali Zafar, who sought information regarding Noreen’s health and her being taken to the hospital. The PML-N senator said Noreen was “immediately provided with medical facilities”. “As per the information available, she is fine and all her medical tests are normal,” he said. On concerns about Noreen’s family allegedly not being allowed to meet her, the prime minister’s adviser said details would also be sought on the matter. He assured the PTI that if this was true, it would be addressed depending on the circumstances at the hospital. The five years from 2020-2025 over which the national feral deer action plan was assessed covers a period in which the famously elusive species has increasingly encroached upon major cities, leading to more frequent encounters – including a memorable occasion in which two men in various degrees of undress were fined after becoming lost in the bush when they were spooked by deer while nude sunbathing . title: Battle lines redrawn in Spain’s snap election after latest train disaster
text: Next month’s poll no longer the contest it was, as Pedro Sánchez finds himself forced to defend government’s safety record One of the most dependable cliches of contemporary Spanish politics is that it never pays to bet against Pedro Sánchez . Time and time again – as leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers’ party (PSOE) and as prime minister – Sánchez has shown an almost preternatural ability to profit from adversity, and to confound expectations and wrongfoot his opponents. But next month’s snap general election , called by Sánchez after rightwing and far-right parties voted down the housing reforms his coalition government had announced in response to angry protests , may suddenly not be the contest it once was. title: Electrocutions, disease and no pay: how workers risk exploitation in Europe’s datacentres
text: As thousands of datacentres are constructed across Europe, the Guardian and Investigate Europe have uncovered disturbing evidence that some workers building them are exposed to dangerous conditions and living in fear of speaking out Sandu* checked his watch. He was winding down the last 15 minutes of his shift at a vast Google datacentre site in Saint-Ghislain, Belgium, in March, when the call came in. The 34-year-old electrical tester had already worked almost 10 hours, but says such last-minute jobs were normal: “I had no choice. People have been fired after saying no.” The task was one Sandu had done many times before and involved a series of tests measuring the safety and integrity of the electrical wiring. A protective suit was locked away in an equipment room. The round trip would have added another 15 minutes to the job, he says, and people were waiting, so he decided not to retrieve the suit. title: Spain begins mourning period as search continues for train crash victims
text: Emergency services, drones and dog unit continue to comb carriages as Civil Guard sets up clinics for relatives to provide DNA samples How did the Spain train crash happen and what will investigators be asking? Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday for at least 69 people who died in a high-speed rail collision, as hospitals continued to treat dozens of injured passengers and train drivers went on strike to urge more investment in railway safety. The trains – one from Spain’s state-owned Renfe and the other from the private rail company Iryo – were travelling from Madrid towards the southern region of Andalucía on Wednesday when they collided just before 9am. After the Iryo train came to a halt, the other slammed into its rear, knocking several carriages off the track near Urda in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha. Continue reading...

title: Elke Sommer, prolific German star of A Shot in the Dark and And Then There Were None, dies aged 85
text: The Berlin-born performer had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the Pink Panther film A Shot in the Dark, early 70s Agatha Christie adaptation And Then there Were None, and British sex comedy Carry on Behind, has died aged 85. Bild magazine reported that Sommer died in Los Angeles of heart failure. German-born Sommer, whose best-known film roles were in the 1960s and 70s, was one of the wave of European performers who crossed over to Hollywood and English-language cinema with considerable success, following the postwar emergence of European new wave cinema. Sommer was one of the few German actors to make waves at the time, as Hollywood made much of her bombshell image. Continue reading...

title: JD Vance letter may offer last chance to avert fresh conflict between US and Iran
text: US vice-president writes to top Iranian security official in sign Washington has not abandoned diplomacy Hopes of averting a major new conflagration between Iran and the US soon after Tuesday’s midterm elections could rest on Iran’s response to a personal letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance, offering to restart diplomacy. The letter, written after predominantly Qatari mediation, was sent to the secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei on Sunday. It requires Tehran to agree to make commitments on its nuclear programme at the start of a process that would lead to the opening of the strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for US sanctions relief. text: Brezilya ulusal telekomünikasyon düzenleyicisi Anatel, ülkedeki 263 milyon mobil abonenin tamamından canlı yüz taraması talep eden zorunlu bir biyometrik kayıt kuralını onayladı. Ulusal veri koruma otoritesinin yüz tanıma verilerini yönetme çerçevesi ise henüz tamamlanmadı.

title: Arabanızın en büyük güvenlik zafiyeti beklenmedik bir yerde olabilir
text: Bir otomobilin eğlence sistemi frenlerine giden bir yol sağlayabilir mi? Güvenlik araştırmacıları 2015 yılında bir Jeep Cherokee'de bu olasılığı gösterdi. Araştırmacılar, araç içi eğlenceyi çalıştıran bilgi-eğlence sistemine uzaktan erişti ve sürüş işlevlerine müdahale etti.

title: Yapay zeka donanımları siber saldırıya uğrayabiliyor: Sohbet robotları tehlikeli yanıtlar veriyor
text: CNN ile özel olarak paylaşılan yeni bir araştırmaya göre, büyük yapay zeka modellerini destekleyen donanımlar bilgisayar korsanlarının hedefi haline gelebiliyor. Bu durum, sohbet robotlarının kullanıcılardan gelen sorulara hatalı ve tehlikeli yanıtlar vermesine yol açıyor.

title: Finlandiya Google'ın veri merkezi alanı için orman temizlemesine cezai soruşturma başlattı
text: Finlandiya polisi, ülkenin kuzey kırsalında planlanan bir Google veri merkezi alanında ülkenin çevre yasalarının olası ihlallerine yönelik cezai soruşturma başlattı.

title: 288 bin ton Rus dizeli taşıyan yedi petrol tankeri ABD'ye doğru yola çıktı
text: Greenpeace tarafından takip edilen tankerler, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ve Vladimir Putin anlaşmasının ilk aşamasını oluşturuyor ancak yüklerini boşaltıp boşaltmayacakları konusunda belirsizlik var.

title: Yapay zeka Google'a 500 milyar dolar kaybettirdi
text: Google'ın ana şirketi Alphabet, perşembe günü ticari operasyonlarına ilişkin yılın son güncellemesiyle Wall Street'i sarsmasının ardından 500 milyar dolardan biraz fazla değer kaybetti.

title: Vücudunuz için en büyük lif kaynakları çöp kutunuzda olabilir
text: İngiltereli araştırmacılar, kabuk ve sap gibi meyve ve sebze artıklarını yemenin çoğumuzun eksikliğini hissettiği bir sağlık artısı sağlayabileceğini belirtti.

text: Kripto para devi Binance, platformunda yaşanan bir güvenlik olayının yaklaşık 6,3 milyar dolar değerindeki varlığı etkilediğini bildirdi.

text: ABD'nin, İsrail'deki seçimlerin ardından Orta Doğu'ya ve İsrail'e askeri bir hava köprüsü operasyonu başlattığı öne sürüldü.

text: Kripto para borsası Binance, olası bir güvenlik sorununa ilişkin inceleme sürerken dondurulan varlıkların doğrulanmış toplam tutarının 2,54 milyar dolar olduğunu bildirdi.

title: İnsanlar fosil yakıtlarla sonraki buzul çağını kazara iptal etti
text: Yapılan yeni bir araştırma, insanlığın fosil yakıt kullanımıyla yarattığı küresel ısınmanın, dünyada başlamak üzere olan yeni bir buzul çağını durdurduğunu ortaya koydu.

title: İran: Şartlarımız üzerinde anlaşmaya varılmadan müzakere olmayacak

title: UKMTO: Hürmüz Boğazı'nda bir tankere bilinmeyen cisim isabet etti
text: İngiltere Deniz Ticaret Operasyonları (UKMTO), Hürmüz Boğazı'nda bir tankere bilinmeyen bir cismin isabet ettiğini bildirdi.

title: Bosna Hersek'te EUFOR'a ait helikopter düştü
text: Bosna Hersek'in kuzeyindeki Brcko'da, Avrupa Birliği (AB) Barış Gücü Misyonuna (EUFOR) ait askeri helikopterin düşmesi sonucu 4 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 11 kişi yaralandı.

title: Putin, Avrupa ile olası savaşta kazanan olmayacağını söyledi
text: Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin, Avrupa ile savaş istemediklerini ancak böyle bir çatışmaya hazır olduklarını belirterek, olası bir savaşta kazanan olmayacağı uyarısında bulundu.

title: İsrail'de sandıktan koalisyon belirsizliği çıkan seçimlerde oy sayımı tamamlandı
text: İsrail'de yapılan ve sandıktan koalisyon belirsizliğinin çıktığı parlamento seçimlerinde oy sayımı tamamlandı.

title: İsrail'deki çocuk istismarı olayıyla ilgili ABD'de gözaltılar yapıldı
text: ABD'de, İsrail'de çocuklara yönelik cinsel istismar suçlarıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen bazı ABD vatandaşlarının gözaltına alındığı bildirildi.

title: BM: İsrail, Ekim 2023'ten bu yana Gazze'de yaklaşık 300 gazeteciyi ve medya çalışanını öldürdü
text: Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Filistin Özel Raportörü Francesca Albanese, İsrail ordusunun, işgal altında tuttuğu Gazze'de, Ekim 2023'ten bu yana yaklaşık 300 gazeteciyi ve medya çalışanını öldürdüğünü ve sonrasında bunların bazılarını "terörist olarak yaftaladığını" belirtti.

title: Suudi Arabistan'ın başkenti Riyad'da saldırı uyarısı sonrası çok sayıda patlama sesi duyuldu
text: Yemen'deki İran destekli Husilerin hedefindeki Suudi Arabistan'ın başkenti Riyad'da saldırı uyarısı sonrası hava savunma sistemleri devreye girdi ve çok sayıda patlama sesi duyuldu.

title: Uluslararası Finans Enstitüsü: Avrupa'nın toplam borcu rekor seviyeye ulaştı
text: Uluslararası Finans Enstitüsü (IIF), Avrupa'da 32 ülkenin toplam borcunun yılın ilk yarısında 95 trilyon doların üzerine çıkarak yeni bir rekora ulaştığını, artan borçlanma maliyetleri ve siyasi belirsizliklerin borç seviyelerini istikrara kavuşturmayı zorlaştırdığını bildirdi.

title: ABD, Güney Koreli bir milletvekiline daha vize vermedi
text: Güney Kore'de iktidardaki Demokrat Parti'den Milletvekili Jin Sung-joon, Hawaii'deki ABD Pasifik Komutanlığı'na düzenlenmesi planlanan parlamento ziyareti kapsamında yaptığı vize başvurusunun Amerika Birleşik Devletleri tarafından reddedildiğini duyurdu.

title: İran basını: Vance'in barış müzakerelerini yeniden başlatmak için gönderdiği mektuba Tahran yanıt vermedi
text: İran basını, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın, "Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance'i İran'la müzakereleri yeniden başlatmakla görevlendirdiği" iddiasını yalanlamasına karşın, Vance'in İran'ın en üst düzey güvenlik yetkilisi Muhsin Rızai'ye gönderdiği mektuba Tahran yönetiminin yanıt vermediğini yazdı.

title: BM: Yapay zeka ve gelişen teknolojiler deniz güvenliği için yeni riskler oluşturuyor
text: Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Genel Sekreteri Antonio Guterres'in Kabine Şefi Courtenay Rattray, yapay zeka ve gelişen teknolojilerin deniz güvenliği alanında yeni fırsatlar sunarken siber saldırılar, yanlış hesaplamalar ve istenmeyen gerilimlerin tırmanması gibi riskleri de beraberinde getirdiğini belirtti.

title: 100 bin simülasyonla test edildi: Kuyruklu yıldızlar Dünya'ya yaşam taşımış olabilir mi?
text: Cambridge Üniversitesi'nden gökbilimcilerin gerçekleştirdiği kapsamlı simülasyonlar, yaşamın temel yapı taşlarını taşıyan kuyruklu yıldızların Dünya'ya çarpma senaryosunun daha önce sanıldığı kadar olası olmadığını ortaya koydu.

title: Von der Leyen, Kanada için ısrarla önerdiği ortak üyelik modelini anlattı
text: Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu Başkanı Ursula von der Leyen, Kanada için ısrarla önerdiği "ortak üyelik" modelinin ayrıntılarını açıklayarak, bu modelin Avrupa dışındaki diğer en yakın ortaklara da açık olacağını bildirdi.

title: Fransız basınından Türkiyeye övgü: Eğitimde üç kat az harcama, daha yüksek PISA puanı
text: Fransa, öğrenci başına eğitim harcamalarında Türkiye'nin yaklaşık üç katına ulaşmasına rağmen 2025 PISA sonuçlarında Türkiye'nin gerisinde kaldı. Yapılan bir analizde, eğitimde başarıyı belirleyen unsurun yalnızca harcama miktarı olmadığını ortaya koydu.

title: İşgalci İsrail ordusu, Batı Şeria'daki baskınlarını sürdürüyor
text: Filistin Esirler Medya Ofisi, İsrail'in işgal altındaki Batı Şeria'da, başta Nablus olmak üzere birçok kente düzenlediği baskınlarda 2 kişiyi darbederek yaraladığını, 3'ü kardeş, 13 kişiyi gözaltına aldığını bildirdi.

title: Pakistan Başbakanı Şerif'ten 29 Ekim Cumhuriyet Bayramı dolayısıyla tebrik mesajı

title: AB, çocukların çevrim içi ortamda korunmasında ortak düzenlemeler hedefliyor

title: Avrupa Merkez Bankası politika faizini sabit tuttu
text: Avrupa Merkez Bankası (ECB), 3 temel politika faizini piyasa beklentileri doğrultusunda sabit tuttu.

title: ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Rubio'dan 29 Ekim Cumhuriyet Bayramı dolayısıyla tebrik mesajı
text: ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio, 29 Ekim Cumhuriyet Bayramı dolayısıyla tebrik mesajı paylaştı.

title: Filistin'den İsrail seçimleri açıklaması: İşgali bitirecek bir ortak çıkmasını umuyoruz
text: Filistin Devlet Başkan Yardımcısı Hüseyin eş-Şeyh, İsrail'de düzenlenen genel seçimlerin "işgale son vermeye ve adil bir barışı sağlamaya inanan bir ortak" çıkarmasını umduklarını belirtti.

title: İran Cumhurbaşkanı Pezeşkiyan: Çevredeki ülkelerle yardımlaşarak bölgemizin güvenliğini sağlayabiliriz
text: İran Cumhurbaşkanı Mesud Pezeşkiyan, çevre ve komşu ülkelerle yardımlaşma suretiyle bölge güvenliğini birlikte sağlayabileceklerini söyledi.

title: AB'den üye ülkelere Ukrayna'ya destek için çağrı
text: Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu, üye ülkeleri, Avrupa'nın savunma kapasitesini güçlendirmek ve Ukrayna'ya desteği artırmak amacıyla "Avrupa Güvenlik Eylemi" (SAFE) mekanizması kapsamında ayrılan 21,3 milyar euroluk kaynağı kullanmaya davet etti.

title: İsrail'de Arap partileri rekor kırdı, 19 milletvekili çıkardı
text: İsrail'de yapılan parlamento seçimlerinin ardından oyların yüzde 93'ünden fazlası sayılırken, İsrail vatandaşı Filistinlileri temsil eden partilerin 19 milletvekili çıkararak rekor kırdığı belirtildi.

title: Putin, Filistin'in unutulmaması gerektiğini söyledi
text: Putin, Basra Körfezi'ndeki gelişmeler nedeniyle Filistin sorununun unutulmaması gerektiğini belirterek, sorunun ancak bağımsız Filistin Devletinin kurulmasını öngören iki devletli çözümle sona erdirilebileceğini belirtti.

title: Fransa'da son eylemlerde bildirilen içeriklerin büyük kısmı sosyal medyadan kaldırıldı
text: Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron, sosyal medya platformlarının ülkedeki son eylemler kapsamında yerel makamlar tarafından bildirilen içeriklerin büyük bir kısmını kaldırdıklarını açıkladı.

title: Avrupa Merkez Bankası Başkanı Lagarde istifa etti
text: Avrupa Birliği (AB) Konseyi Başkanı Antonio Costa, Avrupa Merkez Bankası (ECB) Başkanı Christine Lagarde'ın 7 Şubat 2027'de görevinden ayrılma niyetini kendisine bildirdiğini açıkladı.

title: İspanya'da 2 hızlı treninin çarpıştığı kazada ölenlerin sayısı 69'a çıktı
text: İspanya'nın Toledo kenti yakınlarında 2 hızlı yolcu treninin çarpıştığı kazada ölenlerin sayısı 69'a yükseldi.

text: Brüksel'deki NATO Karargahı ve dünyanın çeşitli yerlerindeki NATO komutanlıklarının resmi hesaplarından paylaşılan mesajlarla, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti'nin kuruluşunun 103. yıl dönümü kutlandı.

title: Gazze'de 21 bin 468 hasta ve yaralı tahliye bekliyor

title: İsrail'de muhalif lider Golan, Netanyahu ile koalisyon hükümeti kurmayacaklarını açıkladı

title: İspanya'da tren faciasının ardından 3 günlük ulusal yas ilan edildi
text: İspanya, bu yıl ikinci kez yaşanan ölümcül yüksek hızlı tren kazasının ardından üç günlük ulusal yas ilan etti. Yakınlarını arayan aileler, sevdiklerinden haber alabilmek için yetkililere başvuruyor.

title: AB, yüksek enerji fiyatları nedeniyle zorlu bir kışa hazırlanıyor
