title: Several people wounded in Israeli strike on tent sheltering displaced Gazans, Wafa reports
text: Several people wounded in Israeli strike on tent sheltering displaced Gazans, Wafa reports Several displaced Gazans were injuries on Thursday evening following an Israeli strike west of Gaza City, Wafa reported. A Wafa journalist said that an Israeli combat drone targeted a tent sheltering displaced people in the al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City, resulting in several casualties who were transferred to al-Shifa Hospital.

title: Saudi Arabia says preparations on for 2027 AFC Asian cup
text: Saudi Arabia says preparations on for 2027 AFC Asian cup Saudi Arabia has said preparations for the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, due to begin on 7 January in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar, remain on schedule despite escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The tournament's local organising committee said that work was continuing in coordination with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), amid concerns over escalation in fighting that has led to postponement of several sporting events. AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa said on Wednesday that a final decision could wait until the end of November and "we could move back a year to 2028 if we need to".

title: 'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu
text: 'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu US President Donald Trump has said he does not trust anybody in politics when asked directly whether he trusts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, weeks before Israel’s parliamentary election. In an interview with Newsmax’s “Finnerty” on Thursday, host Rob Finnerty asked whether he trusted Netanyahu. “I don’t trust anybody, honestly,” Trump replied. “I don’t trust anybody. In the world of politics, I don’t trust anybody,” Trump repeated. He did not say whether he had any particular concerns about Netanyahu, with whom he has kept a close political and military partnership. Asked whether he planned to get involved in the 27 October election, in which Netanyahu is seeking another term, Trump said: "Well, they'd like me to be. Yeah, they'd like me to be." He added: “I’ve had a very good relationship with him. We’ve had good success together.” Trump has previously held back from endorsing Netanyahu. In a Time interview published on 1 October, he said his “primary thing” was to help defend Israel.

title: Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM
text: Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM Iraq’s parliament has approved Laith al-Khazali, a senior figure from the Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq movement, as a deputy prime minister. The United States designated the group a "foreign terrorist organisation" in 2020. Khazali is the brother of the movement’s leader, Qais al-Khazali. Washington designated both brothers as "specially designated global terrorists", citing attacks including a 2007 assault that killed five US soldiers. The US Treasury also sanctioned them in 2019 over the killing of protesters in Iraq. Lawmakers on Thursday approved three deputy prime ministers and 11 ministers, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The appointments include Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister. Zaidi's government has pledged economic reforms, anti-corruption measures and efforts to strengthen state institutions — but faces steep challenges, including rebuilding an economy battered by regional instability, tackling endemic corruption, and reining in Iran-allied armed groups, according to Reuters. Lawmakers approved 11 portfolios, including Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister. (Reuters)

title: Houthis claim Saudi reconnaissance drone downed over Marib
text: Houthis claim Saudi reconnaissance drone downed over Marib Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree has said the group shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone over Marib governorate. In a statement posted on Telegram, Saree said the drone had been carrying out “hostile activities” in the governorate’s airspace. Earlier, Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack on the government headquarters in Aden, with Saree describing the building as housing "Saudi war operations room".

title: Saudi-led coalition destroys drone headed towards Eastern Province, spokesman says
text: Saudi-led coalition destroys drone headed towards Eastern Province, spokesman says A drone launched towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province was intercepted and destroyed, Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Major General Turki al-Maliki said, without specifying the source of the drone and whether it caused any damage, according to Al Jazeera. Earlier, Houthis claimed the deadly attack on the Saudi-backed Yemeni government's headquarters in Aden.

title: Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue
text: Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue US President Donald Trump has said he is weighing fresh strikes on Iran without nuclear weapons or ground troops, while insisting negotiations with Tehran were under way. Asked on Newsmax’s “Finnerty” on Thursday about reports he is considering the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, the “mother of all bombs”, possibly after the 3 November midterms, Trump said it is “not nuclear at all”. He called it “just an extremely large bomb”. CNN reported that the US military has drawn up plans to use the roughly 21,600-pound MOAB against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if Trump orders renewed combat. Asked if that would involve American ground troops, he said: “No, I don’t see that.” He said that withdrawing now risks having to “do it again” within a year, reiterating "Iran must never get a nuclear weapon". Trump predicted the war “will be over very soon”, adding that “they are negotiating with us”. He said the end would come “one way or the other”. “They’ve asked us to please stop. And we do, because we’re negotiating with them,” he said.

title: China says Israel should stop 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements
text: China says Israel should stop 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of West Bank settlements, China's foreign ministry said in a statement on Friday. China has consistently held that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century, Wang told Herzog during a meeting in Azerbaijan, the ministry added. Wang said that promoting peace and reconciliation in the region is the "cornerstone" of China's Middle East policy China believes that the "two-state solution" is the right path to a resolution and the immediate priority is to fully open access to the Gaza Strip so a humanitarian "catastrophe" is not allowed to spread, Wang added China is willing to work with the international community to push all parties to return to dialogue and consultation as soon as possible and seek a political settlement of the conflict, Wang added Report by Reuters

title: Saudi Arabia calls Houthi attacks on civilian facilities 'full-fledged war crimes'
text: Saudi Arabia calls Houthi attacks on civilian facilities 'full-fledged war crimes' Saudi Arabia's Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed Elkhereiji has said Houthi attacks on civilian, economic and airport facilities in the kingdom “constitute full-fledged war crimes”. "Elkhereiji noted the militia's attacks had crossed all ethical and religious boundaries by deliberately targeting Makkah, Madinah, Umrah performers, and visitors," Saudi Press Agency said in a statement. The minister made these remarks at the outset of his meeting with ambassadors of European and African countries to the kingdom, SPA said. He also affirmed that Saudi Arabia "would not relent in protecting its citizens, residents, or visitors, and would take all legitimate measures to defend its territory, repel aggression, and deter aggressors". SPA reported that the ambassadors reiterated their countries' condemnation of the attacks against the kingdom and expressed their countries' solidarity. Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed Elkhereiji said the kingdom would take all legitimate measures to "repel aggression, and deter aggressors". (Courtesy SPA)

title: Baqaei hits back at Miliband over 'Iranian aggression' remarks

title: Houthis claim attack on government headquarters, call it 'Saudi war room'
text: Houthis claim attack on government headquarters, call it 'Saudi war room' Yemen's Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attack on the government headquarters in Aden, with its spokesperson, Yahya Saree, describing the building as housing "Saudi war operations room". Saree said any Saudi military or economic presence on Yemeni land would be a legitimate target of the armed forces. The country's Prime Minister Shaya Zindani, who was not injured in the attack, condemned the Houthis' attack on Aden, calling it "cowardly" and a "continuation of their criminal behaviour". He vowed that it would not weaken the resolve of its forces to continue operations against the Houthis on Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and other front lines.

In May 2024, it launched AI Overviews, where Google generates summarised answers to search queries, rather than only showing links as it historically did. Then, in March 2025, Google added AI Mode, which opens in a separate window and provides a more comprehensive answer and more links than AI Overviews. Now, contextual links will be featured more “more frequently” and higher up in AI-generated search content. Google will also expand worldwide its link “carousel,” which is cards displayed directly below AI Overviews that show headlines with images for relevant articles. The algorithm will prioritise articles from sites a user has previously identified as “preferred sources,” and it will also be able to pull in content from relevant social media posts and other forums. Google will also make links displayed at the end of AI-generated summaries “more engaging and prominent” for users who want to “dig deeper.” During its second-quarter 2025 results, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said that AI Overviews had more than two billion monthly users in over 200 countries. text: • Pezeshkian decries US blockade, insists ‘military force’ will not compel Tehran into submission • Washington weighs using ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ against Iranian energy sites, CNN reports WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump once again predicted a swift end to the war with Iran, and a sharp drop in oil prices once the conflict concludes, even as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force them into submission. “The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana. “They’ll never have a nuclear weapon, and oil prices will drop like a rock.” According to Anadolu Agency , Trump also expressed uncertainty over which Ira­nian officials the US was negotiating with. “They don’t have a navy. title: IHC seeks PTI response in case about Imran’s X account
text: ISLAMABAD: The Isla­mabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday granted PTI interim chairman Barris­ter Gohar Ali Khan additional time to submit a written response to a petition seeking a ban on party founder Imran Khan’s official X account, adjourning the hearing until Nov 23. Justice Arbab Muham­mad Tahir heard the petition, filed by Ghulam Mur­taza, while Barrister Gohar appeared in person. The court observed that Barrister Gohar could have submitted his response in writing. The PTI leader told the court his party did not cla­im ownership of the X ac­­c­ount in question. However, citing a change in circumstances, he sought additional time to submit a detailed response. Meanwhile, Judicial Magistrate Shaista Kundi issued arrest warrants for the accused who failed to appear in cases registered against the PTI founder and others in connection with the 2014 sit-in. Mr Khan could not be produced in court as he is currently incarcerated in Adiala jail. The magistrate then adjourned proceedings till Nov 25 and directed that evidence be presented at the next hearing. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

title: Two killed as rain, snow disrupt life across Gilgit-Baltistan
text: • Babusar Pass road closed to all traffic; Diamer police rescue tourists stranded after heavy snowfall • Karakoram Highway remains open despite blockages along route GILGIT: Two young men were killed on Thursday when a landslide struck their vehicle on the Karakoram Highway, as intermittent rain and snowfall disrupted routine life across Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and blocked the Babusar Pass road and other links to remote areas. Local police said Arif Hussain and Kashif Ali, residents of Gul­mat in the Nagar district, were travelling on Karakoram High­way when a rock struck their vehicle in a landslide-prone area near the Pissan section, early on Thursday. Both men were seriously inj­u­red and later succumbed to their injuries. They were shifted to a nearby government hospital, where doctors pronounced them dead. According to the local administration, rain caused landslides at multiple locations in the Nagar section on Wednesday and Thursday. “Heavy rain is currently continuing in the Nagar district, leading to landslides at various locations along the Karakoram Highway. However, the highway remains open to traffic,” a GB police spokesperson said. “The public is advised to contact the Police Helpline at 15 to check the latest status of the highway before travelling.” Meanwhile, authorities said upper areas of GB received intermittent snowfall, while lower areas received rain. “The Babusar Pass road has been temporarily closed to all traffic due to heavy snowfall at Babusar Top,”

text: MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq has called for a broad-based consensus on the future of refugee seats in the assembly, urging political leaders to help resolve the current crisis through dialogue and reforms. Speaking to journalists at the Speaker House on Thursday, Mr Fa­­rooq said political leaders had an opportunity to align themselves with national objectives and provide guidance by finding a way forward rather than dwelling on the past. “Learning from mistakes is wisdom. We need to explore new avenues for the future,” he said, adding that he supported reforms in all institutions. AJK could not progress with its large administrative structure and high expenditure, he said, while maintaining that the newly elected government, comprising young people, should be given an opportunity to move in the right direction. Backs institutional reforms, says electricity and flour subsidies will continue He also said subsidies on electricity and flour would not be withdrawn, though relief and concessions should be targeted on the basis of data. text: KARACHI: A sealed report prepared by the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in Mir Raza Ali’s murder investigation was handed over to the provincial government on Thursday. The commission, headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court, concluded its proceedings last week after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings, including inspection of the crime scene. The inquiry report along with associated documents was handed over to focal person of the provincial government and additional secretary of home department Javed Ahmed Abro by registrar of the commission Abdul Majid on the premises of the SHC. As Justice Sial was hearing cases at the SHC Hyderabad circuit court, the registrar of the commission handed over the sealed report along with the entire record of the proceedings to the provincial authorities. It’s up to provincial authorities whether to make the document public or keep it secret, says official According to a communication sent by registrar Abdul Majid to the chief minister of Sindh through the focal person, since Justice Sial has been sitting at SHC Hyderabad pursuant to the roster commencing from Oct 12, the registrar has handed over the sealed report to the focal person along with executive summary, statements of witnesses and other supplementary documents. title: PTA shares tips to improve calls, internet quality
text: • Urges users to turn on 4G/LTE, VoLTE settings on their phones • Consumers with older SIM cards told to upgrade for 4G support ISLAMABAD: The Pak­i­stan Telecommu­nica­tion Authority (PTA) adv­ised mobile phone users on Thursday to adjust their network settings and adopt newer technologies, including Voice over Long-Term Evolution (VoLTE), Wi-Fi Calling, and VoWiFi, to improve their calling and mobile internet experience. Responding to consumer complaints regarding unclear voice quality and connection delays on 4G and LTE calls, the telecom regulator recommended that users verify their handset network settings and activate the 4G/LTE option if it is not already switched on. The authority urged consumers to enable VoLTE, Wi-Fi Calling and VoWiFi options on their phones, noting that the availability and use of these facilities depend on compatibility between the handset and the relevant mobile operator. The guidance is primarily relevant to regions where 4G service is expanding following a recent spectrum auction. According to the regulator, VoLTE enables voice calls over a 4G network, which improves voice quality and speeds up call connections. To benefit from the facility, however, the handset, the SIM card and the mobile operator must all support the technology. For areas where mobile signals are weak, such as inside homes or in basements, the authority said Wi-Fi Calling and VoWiFi could be particularly useful. title: Textile exports rise
text: ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan’s textile and clothing exports rose 5.26 per cent to $5.026 billion in the first quarter of 2026-27 from $4.775bn in the same period last year. The marginal rise in export proceeds was attributed to elevated input costs, which eroded exporters’ competitiveness, and external shocks that disrupted shipments, according to data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics released on Thursday. Textile exporters have already warned the government that exports could slow further in the second quarter if no corrective measures are taken. Two major setbacks mainly contributed to slowing exports — suspension of trade with Afghanistan since October 2025 and falling exports to the Middle East due to the prevailing war in the region, especially the United Arab Emirates. PBS data showed readymade garment exports surged 15.69pc in value and 17.38pc in quantity during July-September FY27, while knitwear rose 4.14pc in value but fell 0.46pc in quantity. By contrast, bedwear dipped 0.07pc in value and 0.71pc in quantity. Pakistan’s oil import bill rose 6.50pc in 1QFY27 to $4.02bn from $3.77bn a year ago. Data showed import of crude oil jumped 23.10pc in value, with a decline of 6.87pc in quantity, indicating that the higher value of crude oil is due to rising international oil prices. The CII members also mentioned the Houthis in a veiled criticism of their intervention in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea. title: FBR extends deadline for filing income tax returns to Oct 31
text: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has further extended the date for filing income tax returns for 2026 to Oct 31. The notification, posted on the FBR’s X account, said: “In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 214A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, the Federal Board of Revenue is pleased to further extend the date of filing of income tax returns for tax year 2026 upto October 31, 2026, in the case of persons who were required to file their returns by September 30, 2026, and whose date of filing had earlier been extended up to October 15, 2026.” It added that the deadline had been extended “in view of requests received from various trade bodies and tax bar associations”. Previously, the board had extended the date to Oct 15, from the original deadline of Sept 30. Trade bodies and professionals had sought an extension of the deadline, citing delays in the issuance of return forms and heavy online traffic as major hurdles in timely filing. Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry President Atif Ikram Sheikh had also formally urged the government to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns to Oct 31 to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers. title: Joint sitting of Parliament endorses emergency, governor's rule in KP amid opposition outcry
text: ISLAMABAD: A joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday gave its approval to the Centre’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid a strong protest from the opposition. The joint session had been summoned to discuss separate resolutions on the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, where the opposition’s PTI was in power. During the session, which was addressed by both members of the treasury and opposition benches, the government justified its decision while the PTI lambasted the Centre and the allegations levelled against the party. The Centre took the measures on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. During Thursday’s joint sitting, opposition members turned up carrying placards inscribed with slogans, such as “emergency na manzoor (emergency is unacceptable)”. PM Shehbaz, who attended part of the session, shook hands with opposition leaders of both the Senate and the NA, pictures and footage showed. title: Modi's predicament: Gen Z pours out on India's streets as dissent surges
text: Despite tens of thousands of security personnel deployed to stop them, youth protesters in India scaled barricades last week, chanted anti-government slogans and scuffled with police officers trying to drag them away. “Long live the revolution,” shouted one young man before police bundled him into a bus. Street protests in India this year are likely to be higher than at any time in the past decade, the independent Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) Project has said, as dissent mounts against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and Gen Z activists pour on to the streets. Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, with people under 30 making up nearly one quarter of the country’s 1 billion voters. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029. title: At UNSC, Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reaffirms support for kingdom's security
text: WASHINGTON: Pakistan on Thursday strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian and economic infrastructure, reaffirming its support for the kingdom’s security and right to self-defence amid escalating regional tensions. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) debate on the Middle East, Pakistan’s acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said, “These attacks must cease immediately.” He reiterated Islamabad’s support for efforts to secure a peaceful settlement in Yemen. Pakistan also backed the UN special envoy’s efforts to resume dialogue aimed at achieving a comprehensive and lasting peace in Yemen. Saudi Arabia has, in recent days, come under sustained attack, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the deadliest in years, as the war with the Houthis dramatically escalates. Yemen’s civil war reignited in July after a UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle East war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets. The conflict in the country has caused what the UN calls one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises , leaving most of the nation’s population dependent on aid. The Saudi-led coalition has fought the Houthis since 2015 after they seized Yemen’s capital Sanaa and forced out the internationally recognised government from the city, until a UN-brokered ceasefire in 2022. title: The Houthis' varied arsenal used to strike Saudi Arabia
text: Yemen’s Houthis have built up a missile and drone arsenal that allows them varied and sustained strike capabilities, as Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government it sponsors are finding out. ‘Tit for tat’ strategy Since early September, the Houthis have hit key oil infrastructure and airports across Saudi Arabia — notably Riyadh’s airport , which has been targeted 20 times. They have also, unsuccessfully, targeted the cities of Madina and Makkah. The trigger for their return to hostilities, after a four-year truce, was a Saudi bombardment of the airport at Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, in July, to prevent a Houthi delegation from landing there. Fighters loyal to the Houthi authorities, take part in a rally to recruit more fighters, in Sanaa on October 7. — AFP Since then, there have been “tit-for-tat” military strikes, said April Longley Alley, a specialist on Yemen at the Washington Institute think tank. “The Houthis framed this campaign as blockade for blockade, airport for airport, escalation for escalation,” she said. title: Minorities in Pakistan continue to face rights violations despite legislative measures to protect them: HRCP
text: LAHORE: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) on Thursday concluded that religious minorities continue to face violations of their fundamental rights — including through the misuse of blasphemy laws, forced marriages and conversions, hate speech and discriminatory practices — despite recent legislative measures aimed at protecting them. In its seventh annual report on freedom of religion, titled “Sanctuary Denied: Freedom of Religion or Belief in 2025/26”, and an accompanying press release, the HRCP highlighted that scores of individuals accused of blasphemy remained in legal limbo, while alleged perpetrators of an “organised entrapment network” had yet to be investigated. The report documented attacks on the Ahmadi community, including two attacks in Chenab Nagar in October 2025 and June 2026, and pointed out “increasingly overt attempts to exclude Ahmadis” from public and commercial life. Girls belonging to Christian and Hindu communities continued to face abductions and forced marriages , compounded by poverty and inadequate police responses, the report said. Discriminatory employment practices, controversial changes to school curricula and the marginalisation of minority concerns in mainstream media further undermined the principle of equal citizenship, it added. At the report’s launch, HRCP Director Farah Zia warned that the state’s approach to religious minorities was becoming increasingly exclusionary, according to the press release issued by the commission. text: A Saudi foreign ministry official on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis in the latest escalation of their fight with the kingdom, adding that it continues to arm and train the group. “Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions,” Dr Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry, said during a virtual briefing with reporters. “We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” he later said. The official said the kingdom however remained in communication with Iran, even if Tehran appeared unwilling to offer concessions. “We continue to have direct communications with Iran,” Krimly told reporters. “Overall, it doesn’t seem yet that the Iranians are able to provide the necessary concessions for a solution.” The official went on to accuse the Houthis of refusing to meet in Oman in recent weeks as fighting ramped up between the two sides. “At the beginning of this escalation, we asked them to meet in Muscat, Oman and they refused,” he added. “This was the last communication which happened a few weeks ago.” The world’s top crude oil exporter has in recent days come under sustained attack, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the deadliest in years, as the war with the Houthis dramatically escalates. title: Partners and equals
text: IT has been nearly a year since I last wrote an opinion piece. This was not really intentional, just a result of a feeling of hopelessness and helplessness that made me question whether writing is an exercise in futility. But recently, I was surprised when an educationist told me that my last piece on the threat to the Margalla Hills wildlife corridor, was put up in their school for students to read. I decided then, that I need to return to writing. And what better day to voice my thoughts than today. Oct 16, 2026, marks the 75th death anniversary of Shaheed-i-Millat Liaquat Ali Khan, the first prime minister of Pakistan, the Quaid-i-Azam’s close friend and supporter, and a stalwart of the independence movement. On that fateful day, he left behind his life partner, Ra’ana, and their two sons, Ashraf and Akber, in their home in Karachi, to fly to Rawalpindi to address the nation. His speech was being aired live by Radio Pakistan . He had been told his life was in danger, but he believed that the message he wanted to give was important enough to face the danger head-on. He never got to address the nation — and his written speech was never allowed to be published. To this day, we can only speculate at what he was going to reveal. title: Persistence of force
text: WHILE the Balochistan insurgency has been simmering for many decades, in recent years, it seems to be spinning out of control. In July this year, Balochistan became the country’s most violent province, replacing KP for the first time. Some sources say there were 176 terrorist attacks, killing 438 people, including 127 security personnel, the highest ever in a month. This consistent increase in the insurgency’s lethality and spread implies a major mismatch between the threat and the measures taken to counter it. One major weakness is the imbalance between using armed force to address the challenge and subordinating the political dimension that sustains it. This begs the question: why do we continue to rely totally on the use of force to combat this insurgency, knowing that it has not worked for decades? Historically, COIN (counter-insurgency) strategies have succeeded only when they struck the right balance between armed force and political measures. At best, force can create the right conditions to end an insurgency, but only politics can use that opening to bring about peace through negotiations. In fact, David Galula, in his book Counterinsurgency Warfare: Theory and Practice, argues that a successful COIN strategy is “80 per cent political and 20pc military”. His “First Law of COIN” is that “the support of the population is as necessary for the counterinsurgent as the insurgent”, and that this support can be achieved only through political measures. title: Deadly classrooms
text: AT LEAST 30 children, most of them younger than 13, and a teacher have died in Peshawar after the roof of their private school collapsed during morning classes. Dozens more were injured, some critically. The victims had arrived at the Al Khair school expecting an ordinary day. Instead, rescue workers spent hours searching through rubble as parents gathered outside. Police say the building was structurally weak and its roof overloaded with additional construction. The owner has been arrested, while an inquiry is under way. These preliminary findings demand scrutiny. So do reports that concerns about the building’s condition had previously been raised. In June, 14 children died when the roof of a tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. Two days later, another school roof collapse in Baghbanpura killed an eight-year-old. Three incidents in a few months should be enough to force an examination of the places where Pakistan’s children are taught. Across the country, schools and tuition centres operate in buildings ill-suited to accommodating large numbers of pupils. In crowded urban neighbourhoods, houses are converted into classrooms, sometimes with additional floors, makeshift rooms, and roofs carrying more weight than they were designed to support. Yet questions about construction quality, structural approvals, and inspections are too often left unanswered until a disaster occurs. title: What options does Indian law provide for CEC’s removal?
text: AMID growing calls for the resignation of India’s top election official Gyanesh Kumar for alleged voter roll manipulation, a key issue has come to the fore: the process of the chief election commissioner’s appointment, resignation and termination. The campaign to remove Gyanesh Kumar from office began after a newspaper report alleged that he was responsible for removing the names of 130 million voters from India’s electoral rolls — a figure slightly higher than Bangladesh’s entire voting population. While the Congress Party, India’s “cockroach” youth movement and others demand Kumar’s resignation, which is simple enough, Kumar’s removal from office is a lengthy and complicated affair, similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge. Article 324 of the Indian constitution, whi­ch deals with the Election Commission, outlines the procedures for removal of the election chief. Article 324 (5) stipulates that the top election official shall not be removed fr­­om office “except in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court”. In India, the CEC is appointed under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. The CEC is appointed by the president. The law stipulates that people who are serving or have served in positions equivalent to a secretary to the Indian government will be eligible. text: Shevaun Haviland argues PM is right to revisit Labour’s EU red lines as current trading relationship is bad for business Repairing the economic damage of Brexit should be the top priority for Andy Burnham as he reconsiders Labour’s red lines on EU membership, the head of one of Britain’s leading business groups has said. Shevaun Haviland, the director general of the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC), said she welcomed the prime minister reopening the Brexit battle lines despite the uncertainty it could create, arguing that the UK’s current trading relationship with the EU was bad for business. title: Number of cloned number plates on UK roads at record high, data shows
text: More than 11,400 drivers last year were fined for offences they did not recognise as RAC says system needs reform The number of reported “cloned” vehicles involved in offences on UK roads has reached a record high, official data shows. More than 11,400 drivers contacted the DVLA last year after being issued with fines for offences they said they did not recognise or accept responsibility for – most of which are believed to be down to cloning, where a number plate is copied fraudulently on similar vehicles to avoid enforcement cameras.
